We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have identified possible disconnections: sulfonamide formation (sulfonyl chloride + aniline) and amide formation (acyl chloride + aniline). The target has two aromatic rings: a tolyl sulfonamide attached to a phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (para-aminophenyl). Actually structure: p-methyl phenyl-sulfonamide attached to another phenyl ring (para) which has a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (para). So we can disconnect at sulfonamide bond: sulfonyl chloride (p-tolylsulfonyl chloride) + aniline (the other aromatic sulfonyl attached ring). The other aromatic ring is a phenyl with a side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2 (an aniline). That side chain can be formed via amide coupling of acryloyl chloride (or trans-α,β-unsaturated acyl chloride) with an aniline (para-aminophenyl). Actually the side chain is trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2 (an aniline). So we can disconnect amide: acryloyl chloride (or trans-2-propenoyl chloride) + 4-aminophenylamine? Wait the amide attaches to aniline (c3ccccc3N). That's an aniline (para? Actually just aniline). So the amide is formed between acryloyl chloride and aniline (aniline). So we need acryloyl chloride (ClC(=O)C=CH2) but the product has trans double bond with phenyl attached to the double bond: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2. Actually the double bond is attached to phenyl ring (the second phenyl). The SMILES: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the phenyl ring (c2) has a side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2. The double bond is attached to the phenyl ring at the carbon of the double bond (aryl-alkene). So the side chain is trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2, where the CH=CH is attached to the phenyl ring at the first carbon (aryl-CH=CH-). So we can disconnect at the C=C bond? Could be formed via Heck coupling of aryl bromide with acrylate? But we have limited steps (max 3). Simpler: start from commercially available 4-methylphenylsulfonyl chloride (p-tolylsulfonyl chloride) and 4-aminophenyl (p-aminophenyl) with acryloyl chloride? Actually we need the phenyl ring bearing the side chain: we could start from 4-bromo-phenyl (or 4-iodo) and do Heck with acrylate then amide formation. But that adds steps.

Goal: 3 steps total. Could be: Step1: Form sulfonamide between p-tolylsulfonyl chloride and the phenyl-sulfonyl-aryl (the other aromatic ring). That other aromatic ring is a phenyl with side chain (C=C-CO-NH-Ph-NH2). So we need that phenyl-sulfonyl precursor (the aryl sulfonyl chloride? Actually we need the aryl sulfonyl chloride to react with aniline). Wait the sulfonamide bond is between the sulfonyl group attached to the tolyl ring and the nitrogen attached to the second phenyl ring. So we need p-tolylsulfonyl chloride (commercial) and the amine: the second phenyl ring bearing the side chain and an NH (the aniline). That amine is 4-(trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2)aniline? Actually the second phenyl ring is attached to the sulfonyl via its nitrogen (sulfonamide). So the second phenyl ring is a phenyl with an NH attached to sulfonyl, and also bearing the side chain at para position? The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to NS(=O)(=O) from the first ring. So the second phenyl has the sulfonamide nitrogen attached to the ring (i.e., the ring is attached to N of sulfonamide). So the second phenyl is an aniline (NH attached to sulfonyl) with a para side chain of trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2. So the amine needed is 4-(trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2)aniline (i.e., 4-(E-2-((4-aminophenyl)carbamoyl)vinyl)aniline). That is not commercially available likely. But we can build it in one step: start from 4-aminophenyl (aniline) and do acylation with acryloyl chloride to give 4-(acrylamido)aniline (i.e., 4-(C=CC(=O)NH)aniline). Then we need to attach the second phenyl (the aniline) to the double bond? Actually the side chain includes another phenyl attached to the amide nitrogen (Nc3ccccc3N). Wait the amide nitrogen is attached to a phenyl with an NH2 substituent (para-aminophenyl). So the amide is between the acryloyl group and 4-aminophenylamine (aniline). So the amide nitrogen is attached to a phenyl that also has an NH2. So the amide is N-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide. So the side chain is trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2. So the amide nitrogen is attached to a phenyl with an NH2 substituent (para). So the amide precursor is 4-aminophenylamine (p-phenylenediamine) reacting with acryloyl chloride to give N-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide. That product is commercially available? Possibly p-phenylenediamine is cheap, acryloyl chloride is cheap. So step1: acylation of p-phenylenediamine with acryloyl chloride to give N-(4-aminophenyl)acrylamide (the side chain). This yields a molecule with an aniline (the other NH2) still free.

Step2: Perform sulfonamide formation between p-tolylsulfonyl chloride and the aniline of the side chain (the free NH2 on the phenyl). That gives the target molecule? Wait we also need the connection of the sulfonamide nitrogen to the second phenyl ring (the phenyl bearing the side chain). The sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the phenyl ring (the second phenyl) via the nitrogen (i.e., the aniline nitrogen). So after step1, we have a molecule: aniline (para) with acryloyl amide attached to the nitrogen (i.e., N-acryloyl-p-phenylenediamine). The free NH2 is at para position on the phenyl. Then reacting that free NH2 with p-tolylsulfonyl chloride yields sulfonamide linking the tolyl sulfonyl to the phenyl. That gives the target? The target also has the tolyl ring attached via sulfonamide to the phenyl (the same phenyl). Yes.

Thus only 2 steps: 1) acylation of p-phenylenediamine with acryloyl chloride (amide formation). 2) sulfonamide formation with p-tolylsulfonyl chloride.

Check commercial availability: p-phenylenediamine (Nc1ccccc1N) is buyable (True). Acryloyl chloride (ClC(=O)C=CH2) is buyable (True). p-tolylsulfonyl chloride (ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C)cc1) is buyable (True). So all leaves are buyable.

Now need to verify templates for these reactions.

We need template IDs for amide formation from acyl chloride + amine. Search for functional_groups_broken: acyl chloride, formed: amide. Let's search.
